proposed_features.description: The overall scale of the bird relative to its perch or environment, distinguishing the large corvids from the smaller passerines.
The geometry of the bill, specifically the length and curvature, which varies significantly between the heavy corvids and the slender passerines.
The contour of the tail feathers when closed, a key differentiator between the wedge-shaped tail of the raven and the rounded or square tails of the others.
The appearance of the feathers on the throat and upper chest, distinguishing the shaggy, spiky feathers of the raven from the smooth plumage of the others.
Whether the bird is a single solid color or exhibits distinct color differences between the head and the body.
The specific coloration of the head, which is a primary identifier for the bicolored species.
The specific coloration of the main body and wings, distinguishing the dark corvids from the lighter-bodied passerine.
The reflectivity of the feathers, distinguishing the iridescent, shiny plumage of the cowbird from the matte finish of the corvids.
The color of the iris, which is a consistent dark feature in the corvids but appears lighter or different in the passerine.
The color of the legs and feet, which are dark in the corvids but appear lighter or grayish in the passerine.
The ratio of body length to height, distinguishing the long, slender passerine from the compact, deep-chested corvids.
The length of the wings relative to the tail, which is longer in the raven and shorter in the cowbird.
The robustness of the bill, distinguishing the heavy, thick bill of the raven from the thinner bills of the others.
The profile of the head, distinguishing the rounded head of the cowbird from the more angular head of the corvids.
